title: Fase F (Father) — Drop 6 confirmed-dead tables + remove ~734 lines orphaned legacy code (Prompt Sequence sub-feature + Project Planning scaffold + phase-1A tables)
design_notes:
Fase F = drop unused tables + remove legacy code so DPMtF-WebUI only contains what's necessary. ORIGINAL PREMISE WAS WRONG: the C-3 audit (handoff 46, scripts/migrate_c3_drop_dead_tables.py) marked 8 zero-row tables KEEP using a SYNTACTIC grep-count test (any code reference = keep). That is a false-positive for liveness — a table can be referenced by dead/orphaned code. The correct test is REACHABILITY: is the referencing code actually called by the frontend or a live route?

Deep reachability audit (6 parallel investigations, 2026-07-07) confirmed 6 of the 8 zero-row tables are DEAD. All 6 had 0 rows, frontend had ZERO calls to their endpoints, and the Spor G commit cb0c7e0 (2026-06-17) had removed the Prompt Sequence Planner UI (1385 lines dpmtf-app.js + 18 lines index.html) leaving the backend orphaned.

THREE DEAD CLUSTERS (all removed in handoff 59):
1. Prompt Sequence sub-feature: prompt_sequences + prompt_sequence_steps + generated_prompts + ~482 lines dead handlers in routers/prompt_compiler.py (lines 221-689). Live endpoints (/compile, /dispatch, /assign-handoff-id, templates, hitrates) preserved.
2. Project Planning sub-feature: project_plans + ~124 lines dead handlers in routers/webui.py (lines 116-231). Live create-webui/* endpoints preserved.
3. Phase-1A scaffold tables: projects + reference_projects (no SQL at all; C-3 'hits' were INI config-key name collisions).

The 2 OTHER zero-row tables (frontend_panels, panel_classifications) are UI/Frontend-governing (routers/panels.py + mcp-light) — KEPT, on the permanent never-drop list.

DROP METHOD: existing scripts/migrate_c3_drop_dead_tables.py rewritten by implementer to use config.get_db_path(), re-audit each candidate (0 rows + no external FK dependents), topologically order drops (children before parents), create timestamped backup before any DROP. SAFE_TO_DROP populated with the 6 tables; docstring verdict corrected (KEEP→DROPPED with reachability rationale). No Fase E-2 needed.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: implementer initially ran init_db.py AFTER the drop, which RECREATED the 6 tables (init_db.py still had the CREATE blocks) — exactly the DB-loss-incident pattern. Implementer caught it, paused on the init_db.py Human-approval gate (CLAUDE.md §10), then proceeded after approval: removed 6 CREATE TABLE blocks + 2 orphaned seed labels (lbl_panel_prompt_sequences, lbl_btn_create_project_plan) from init_db.py. Re-ran drop; 6 tables confirmed DROPPED and stay gone.

VERDICT (2026-07-07 13:00): APPROVED by review02pay. ~734 lines dead code excised total (~482 prompt_compiler.py + ~124 webui.py + ~131 init_db.py). All validation PASS: py_compile, node --check, init_db.py idempotent, migration idempotent, /api/health healthy, innerHTML clean, no hardcoded paths, requirements unchanged. 6 files changed (4 code + dpmtf.db binary + cycle-state tracking artifact). Human may commit as-is.

DB BACKUPS: pre-handoff59-20260707_120638.bak (Architect, 851968 bytes) + pre-c3-20260707T102251Z.bak + pre-c3-20260707T102636Z.bak (implementer's drop-script). All 6 dropped tables were 0 rows — no data loss.

Handoff 59 showed the value: init_db.py recreated dropped tables on re-run until its CREATE blocks were also removed — a migration system would make this automatic.

Reachability-based dead-code audit method (used in handoff 59) supersedes the syntactic grep-count method of handoff 46's C-3 audit. Future dead-table audits MUST use reachability (frontend caller? live route? writer reachable?) not raw grep counts.
